newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY BILL TO PERMIT TOBACCO, ALCOHOL, DRUG ADS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY BILL TO PERMIT TOBACCO, ALCOHOL, DRUG ADS.

text.p: The Hungarian cabinet has given its approval to a proposed legislation that would allow drug, alcohol and tobacco ads in the non-electronic media, government spokesman Elemer Kiss said.
"The cabinet heard and accepted a proposed law on commercial advertising," he told reporters at a news conference.
The bill would not apply to the broadcast media, which is regulated by the 1995 Media Law, Kiss added. The media law bans tobacco, but not alcohol advertising.
The proposed law would bar certain forms of hidden advertising as well as ads that violate public morals, Kiss said. He did not elaborate.
A statement distributed at the news conference also listed guns, ammunition and explosives as goods that could not be advertised.
Prescription drugs could only be promoted through literature directed at doctors, while non-prescription drugs could be advertised to the general public, the statement added.
The statement said that strict limits would be applied against outdoor and printed press ads that promote alcohol and tobacco use. Neither it, nor Kiss elaborated.

Health activist groups last year told Reuters they were lobbying against all forms of alcohol and tobacco advertising but were facing an uphill battle as alcohol and tobbaco taxes generated 57 billion forint state revenues in 1995.
Kiss said the proposal would soon be submitted to Parliament.
